metric_rationale: This is the within-subject OLS slope of TTB-consistent choice on whether tallying opposes, ties, or supports the TTB winner. TTB predicts the same probability of choosing its winner in all three categories, so its expected slope is zero regardless of beta or lapse rate. Tallying predicts a strong positive gradient: low TTB agreement when the tally opposes TTB, exactly 0.5 at tally ties, and high agreement when tallying supports TTB. Collapsing tally margins to their sign is deliberate: it preserves the robust categorical disagreement while avoiding sensitivity to softmax saturation at large beta. The slope uses nearly all 96 trials and removes each subject's overall tendency to follow TTB through centering, yielding substantially lower between-subject variance than a raw accuracy score or a contrast based on only one trial pair.

This is signed choice alignment with Tallying, restricted to the maximally diagnostic trials where Tallying and Take The Best predict opposite winners. It ranges from -1 to +1: positive values indicate choices following the tally winner, while negative values indicate choices following the highest-validity discriminating cue. In this design, half of the unique pairs—and their exact reversals—are such conflict trials, yielding 48 observations per subject. Tallying predicts a positive expectation approximately (1-epsilon)*tanh(beta), whereas TTB predicts a negative expectation approximately -(1-epsilon)*tanh(beta/2). Thus the theories lie on opposite sides of zero rather than differing only in degree. Exact A/B reversals remove side bias, and averaging all conflict-trial repetitions keeps the per-subject variance low. The metric is linear across observations, so its pooled value remains compatible with its single-subject interpretation.

This metric records whether the subject's aggregate choices fall above or below chance in following the highest-validity discriminating cue. It is side-invariant because the lexical winner is recomputed after each A/B reversal. TTB predicts positive polarity: response noise can weaken preference for the first discriminator but cannot systematically reverse it. Rank-Budget Arbitration predicts negative polarity because retrieval failure is more likely than not at the designed loads, and its pooled rule favors the option opposite the first cue on every stimulus. The polarity transformation targets this qualitative crossover while suppressing between-subject variation in beta, sensitivity, and lapse that mainly changes the magnitude of preference. It remains meaningful for both pooled data and individual-subject slices.

This metric is mean choice alignment with the equal-weight cue-majority direction on the 12 non-tie stimulus structures. It ranges from -1 to 1. Crucially, the design contains equal numbers of majority/lexicographic agreement and majority/lexicographic conflict structures, including exact A/B reversals. Under Take The Best, majority-alignment scores are positive on agreement trials and equally negative on conflict trials, so symmetric response noise leaves their expected mean at zero regardless of beta or epsilon. Under Rank-Budget Arbitration, the rank-retrieval component still cancels across those balanced structures, whereas the pooling component aligns choices with the majority in both classes. The resulting expectation is therefore substantially positive, approximately the pooling probability times response reliability. Each subject contributes 72 diagnostic trials, yielding a stable within-subject estimate while excluding tally ties that contain no directional pooling prediction.

This metric is the post-acquisition cue-majority choice rate. It scores choices relative to the majority winner computed from each display, so the eight A/B reversals cancel response-side preferences. The first eight trials are excluded because Ecological Encoding Hysteresis should have crossed its dense-ecology threshold by then; it subsequently predicts frequent compressed pooling and therefore majority choices. Rank-Budget Arbitration has no history dependence at the fixed load and retains a substantially larger lexicographic component, which favors the opposite option on every trial. Using 88 late trials per subject provides a large categorical gap while keeping binomial between-subject noise low.

This is the observed rate of choosing the winner under sign-compressed, equal-weight pooling. In every designed comparison, that winner is opposite the winner selected by the highest-validity discriminating cue. Rank-Budget Arbitration predicts frequent trial-local rank-retrieval failure and hence a majority-choice rate above 0.5, whereas Ecological Encoding Hysteresis should retain ordered search in this globally sparse block and produce a much lower rate. Pooling all 96 binary observations yields a stable subject-level estimate, and the exact A/B reversals prevent response-side preference from masquerading as majority-rule use.

The metric is the post-initialization proportion of choices favoring the option supported by the unweighted majority of experts. On every designed display, that option is opposed to the winner of the perfectly valid leading cue. Ecological Encoding Hysteresis should rapidly enter its dense-ecology compressed regime and therefore produce a high, stable majority-choice rate across the remaining 92 trials. Relational Coalition Consolidation's dominance safeguard should instead preserve the leading-cue option, producing a much lower rate. Dropping only the first four trials removes the advocated theory's short and parameter-sensitive transition while retaining enough Bernoulli observations per subject to keep between-subject variance small. The statistic is an ordinary observable choice contrast rather than a direct readout of either theory's latent variables.

The metric is 1.25 times the coalition-choice rate over the final 32 trials minus 0.25 times its rate over the first 8 trials. It therefore primarily measures stable late-block coalition capture while adding a smaller, pre-specified reward for acquisition. Relational Coalition Consolidation predicts high late coalition choice and an early-to-late increase as the recurrent Experts 2–4 relation becomes accessible. Ecological Encoding Hysteresis predicts persistent highest-validity-cue choices because the constant discrimination density remains below its pooling threshold, yielding both a low late coalition rate and little temporal change. Coding choices relative to Expert 1 removes A/B side reversals, and averaging many late trials keeps the per-subject statistic stable.

This is the within-position slope of choosing the four-cue majority on the advertised-validity strength of that majority coalition. Coalition strength is computed from log-odds diagnosticity and converted to its four ordinal levels, avoiding excessive leverage from the strongest expert. Ecological Encoding Hysteresis discards lower-cue validity magnitudes once lexical and tally directions are fixed, so it predicts a slope near zero. Contextual Margin Arbitration retains aggregate validity support in both route accessibility and evidence, predicting a positive slope. Residualizing the coalition rank within six-trial serial strata removes the advocated theory's potentially steep context trajectory and substantially reduces randomization-induced between-subject variance. Residualization against majority side also removes incidental response-side imbalance. The pooled result is the mean subject slope, making the same estimand valid for pooled and single-subject inputs.

This is the serial-position-stratified difference in probability of following the highest-validity expert between 6-4 displays (normalized margin 0.20) and all larger opposing majorities (margins 0.40–0.80). Contextual Margin Arbitration places its margin threshold between 0.20 and 0.40, so the 6-4 displays preferentially retain the lexical route while larger majorities strongly activate compression; it therefore predicts a positive contrast. Ecological Encoding Hysteresis uses sign-normalized pooled evidence and has identical density on every display, so it predicts no margin-class contrast. Residualizing the margin-class indicator within 12-trial subject-specific bins removes the pronounced common density-acquisition trajectory and reduces variance caused by random trial order. Pooling the three larger-margin classes also gives 36 versus 60 observations per subject, making the contrast substantially more stable than an endpoint-only slope.
